about: The read-only checks of KEY-KEEP.md section 2.1, with their results as KEY-KEEP.md records them (section 9: check 1; section 10: checks 2 and 3). The device mode writes the two key-record sectors of backup only when every check here has passed: true, with evidence and a source. A condition goes into the plan's gate. Changing this file changes the binary, so it is a reviewed change.

checks.what: the content of backup on a unit: the whole partition and both record sectors (30720, 32767) empty
checks.evidence: unit 2, 2026-10-31, read-only in a RAM image: mmcblk0p15 start 446464, 32768 sectors, all zero (sha256 080acf35...), both record sectors zero (KEY-KEEP.md section 9)

checks.what: no reader or writer of backup in the boot chain: the userdebug U-Boot and trust do not name backup
checks.evidence: offline, 2026-10-31, firmware 1.0.0.94, 1.0.6.20 and 1.0.0.98: U-Boot and trust never name backup and hold no address of it (strings, the 23 partition lookups by name, the backup LBAs as data words and mov/movk values); vbmeta and dtbo do not name it. U-Boot writes backup only when a person asks it from the host (fastboot flash/erase, rockusb by LBA)

checks.what: no writer of backup in Android 1.0.0.94 and 1.0.6.20: fstabs, init rc files, the recovery, the Crestron updater
checks.evidence: offline, 2026-10-31, firmware 1.0.0.94, 1.0.6.20 and 1.0.0.98: no fstab, init rc file, update_engine, uncrypt, vold, bootctl, libwebupdate.so, libprovdetect.so or prov_install table names backup; in normal use (boot, web UI, XiO and USB-disk updates, factory reset, OTA) nothing writes it. The one exception: the Rockchip SD-card update in the recovery, which only a vendor-signed SD update card starts; Android and the network cannot start it
checks.condition: pass with one condition (KEY-KEEP.md section 10.3): if a vendor-signed SD update card is ever used on a unit, read backup again before trusting the record
